items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a formal algebraic space X over a scheme, a reduced algebraic space X_red together with a representable morphism to X which is a thickening, and asserts that morphisms from a reduced algebraic space into X factor uniquely through it (statement lines 2832-2838). The proof has three parts. The affine case is settled by writing the affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes whose transition morphisms are thickenings, so that all stages have isomorphic reductions; representability and the thickening property follow from the covering-by-thickenings lemma and from closure of thickenings under composition, and the author explicitly leaves the verification of the universal property to the reader, pointing at the four statements that make it routine (proof lines 2840-2854). The global case is a glueing construction: for the chosen affine presentation of X one takes the reductions of the members, observes that the fibre products of a reduction with a member are etale over that reduction and therefore reduced, so that the projections factor through the reductions of the members, identifies the resulting fibre products in three ways, and concludes that the two projections form an etale equivalence relation whose quotient is an algebraic space by the presentation theorem; the comparison diagram with the presentation is cartesian, and representability and the thickening property of the resulting morphism are then transferred along a surjective etale morphism by a bootstrap lemma and a descent lemma for representable transformations (proof lines 2856-2890). The third part proves the universal property in general: for a morphism from a reduced algebraic space, the fibre products with the members of the presentation are etale over the source and hence reduced, so each factors through the corresponding reduction, and since those fibre products form an etale covering of the source, the morphism itself factors through X_red (proof lines 2892-2907). The claim is H3: the affine computation, the equivalence-relation glueing with its three-way identification, the transfer of representability and of the thickening property along a cover, and the general universal property are four independent pieces of work.
